result.title: Every Camera Grows Up: Camera-Height Regression in Interactive Video World Models
result.summary: Interactive video world models serve as simulators for embodied agents: from a starting image and an action trajectory, they generate the views the agent would see. The starting image fixes how high the camera is, for example 0.15 m for a floor robot or 2.2 m for an overhead camera, and a faithful simulator must keep this height as the camera moves. We show that six recent open-weight models fail to do so: as motion replaces the starting view with generated content, they move the camera toward human eye level, a failure we call camera-height regression. Our benchmark, EyeHeight, pairs six rendered elevations (0.15 m to 2.2 m) and four calibrated real-world rig heights with scale-free multi-view height estimation. All six models lose their initial height during a $180^\circ$ turn-and-walk rollout: initialized at 0.15 m, only 0-20% of clips end within $1.3\times$ of the starting height as inferred viewpoints converge to human heights of 1.1 m to 1.5 m, whereas ground-truth renders remain within a few percent. In Matrix-Game models, homography-tracked floor motion stays consistent with constant elevation during rotation even as newly outpainted room geometry yields a higher reconstructed viewpoint. Regression grows with rotation angle, begins while the start frame remains in context, and largely reverses in SANA-WM when a $360^\circ$ turn restores the initial view. We trace this pull to human-centric video priors in which floor-level views are nearly absent: in SANA-WM, textual height cues and dense floor-disparity maps do not prevent it, whereas classifier-free text guidance during the first half of denoising strengthens it. Combining unguided sampling with height-balanced fine-tuning recovers more retention but costs 5 MUSIQ points, a loss fixed during those same early steps. Viewpoint drift alone shifts the paths predicted by visual navigation policies.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 EyeHeight 基准，用多视角相机高度估计检验六个开源交互视频世界模型在转身行走时能否保持初始相机高度，发现普遍向人眼高度「回归」，并将其归因于以人为中心的视频先验，尝试用无引导采样与高度均衡微调缓解。
AI.relevance_reason: 相机高度这种需在生成过程中持续维持的几何状态被先验覆盖，可能为 LVR 中「任务必要视觉/几何信息是否在 latent 状态中被先验冲淡」提供可核查的评测与归因思路；视角漂移改变视觉导航策略预测路径，也提示状态误差会传导至决策，但该文并非 VLM 推理方法。
